validated_results.title: Total fluid intake and use of individual beverages and risk of renal cell cancer in two large cohorts.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort analysis reporting pooled multivariate relative risk for alcohol intake and incident renal cell cancer.

extraction.population: Nurses' Health Study women and Health Professionals Follow-up Study men

sample_size.excerpt: Among 88,759 women followed for 20 years in the Nurses' Health Study, and 47,828 men followed for 14 years in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study, we documented 248 incident cases of renal cell cancer.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 88759 + 47828 = 136587

cases.excerpt: Among 88,759 women followed for 20 years in the Nurses' Health Study, and 47,828 men followed for 14 years in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study, we documented 248 incident cases of renal cell cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Alcohol intake was marginally inversely associated with renal cell cancer risk; compared with nondrinkers, the pooled multivariate RR for > or = 15 g/d was 0.66 (95% confidence interval, 0.43-1.00; P, test for trend = 0.07).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Alcohol intake was marginally inversely associated with renal cell cancer risk; compared with nondrinkers, the pooled multivariate RR for > or = 15 g/d was 0.66 (95% confidence interval, 0.43-1.00; P, test for trend = 0.07).

comparison.excerpt: compared with nondrinkers, the pooled multivariate RR for > or = 15 g/d

design.excerpt: We prospectively examined the associations between total fluid and beverage intakes and risk of renal cell cancer.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: We assessed consumption of beverages every 2 to 4 years using a validated semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
